description: Stereo waveguide synthesizer: air driven into a chamber vibrates a spring-loaded piston, and pressure waves travelling down a resonant tube become the stereo output

params.text: Sets the rate at which air is forced into the chamber, which is how hard the instrument is blown
Sets how quickly vibrations reflecting back and forth in the tube die out; larger values reverberate longer
Sets the rotation applied to the stereo polarization of pressure reflected from the far end of the tube
Sets the strength of the piston spring; a stiffer spring vibrates faster
Sets the diameter of the valve the air escapes through; narrow settings turn small piston movements into large changes of escape rate and sound shriller, wide settings sound more mellow
Sets the height of the escape valve against the piston's travel; higher settings need more chamber pressure before air escapes into the tube
Sets the resonant frequency of the tube by making it longer or shorter, marked in Hz; it is not a volt per octave control
Sets the angular rotation given to the polarization of air entering the tube
Attenuates and inverts the airflow CV
Attenuates and inverts the decay CV
Attenuates and inverts the angle CV
Attenuates and inverts the spring CV
Attenuates and inverts the width CV
Attenuates and inverts the centre CV
Attenuates and inverts the root frequency CV
Attenuates and inverts the vortex CV
Sets the volume of the stereo output; it glows red while the output limiter is reducing gain

inputs.text: Varies the rate air is forced into the chamber
Varies how quickly reflections in the tube die out
Varies the stereo rotation applied to reflected pressure
Varies the stiffness of the piston spring
Varies the diameter of the escape valve
Varies the height of the escape valve against the piston's travel
Varies the resonant frequency of the tube
Varies the rotation given to air entering the tube

In VENT mode a level above 1V opens the chamber, letting the air out and cutting off the audio inputs, and it closes again below 0.1V. Clicking the word VENT switches to SEAL, which inverts that logic
Left audio injected into the resonant tube, where it mixes with the pressure from the piston; only DECAY, ANGLE and ROOT act on it, and those control groups light up while a cable is patched
Right audio injected into the resonant tube, where it mixes with the pressure from the piston; only DECAY, ANGLE and ROOT act on it, and those control groups light up while a cable is patched

outputs.text: Left audio out, the real part of the complex tube pressure
Right audio out, the imaginary part of the complex tube pressure

notes: all eleven input ports set the polyphony: the one with the most channels sets the channel count of both outputs, and an input with fewer channels repeats its last channel across the rest
menu: Output limiter — sets an automatic gain control threshold from 1V to 10V, 4V by default, or turns it off at the far right; the OUT knob glows red while it is reducing gain
Toggle VENT/SEAL — inverts the sense of the vent input, doing by menu what clicking the VENT label does
Limiter warning light — turns off the red glow on the OUT knob without turning the limiter off
Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
